title: Plan International CEO visits Cox's Bazar, meets education minister
excerpt: Reena Ghelani discussed child marriage and girls' schooling with the government. No funding or agreement was announced.
content:
From the sector: this story is based on a Plan International press release, edited and attributed by Devlens.

Reena Ghelani, chief executive of Plan International, visited Bangladesh on 10 and 11 November and met the State Minister for Primary and Mass Education, Bobby Hajjaj, to discuss girls' education and child marriage, according to a press release published by The Business Standard on 13 November.

Where she went and who she met

  • Cox's Bazar: Rohingya camps, education and child protection programmes and a community learning centre, where she met children, adolescent girls, young women, parents and volunteer teachers.
  • Dhaka: Ivo Freijsen, UNHCR Representative in Bangladesh; Joris van Bommel, Ambassador of the Netherlands; and Susan Ryle, Australian High Commissioner.
  • Ministry meeting: with Mr Hajjaj and senior officials of the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education. Kabita Bose, Plan International Bangladesh country director, and Ram Kishan, the organisation's Asia Pacific regional director, also took part.

According to the release, the meeting covered primary education and foundational skills, preventing child marriage, keeping girls in secondary school, safer schools with separate toilets, and climate resilience. Plan International said it was ready to support government priorities and Ms Ghelani expressed interest in joint initiatives. No funding or agreement was announced.

Programmes named

  • Steps to a Bright Tomorrow: Education for Adolescents and Youth in Cox's Bazar, run with Jagoroni Chakra Foundation.
  • Girl Shine and Champions of Change.
  • Girls Shaping Climate Solutions: Her Climate, Her Voice, Her Action, including the Durbar Konnya programme.

The release cites UNHCR data for September 2026: more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, over 1.17 million of them in Cox's Bazar, with women and girls about 51% and children more than half.

Why it matters

Visits by INGO chief executives often come before decisions on country budgets and new programmes. With Rohingya funding shrinking, education partners in the camps and local NGOs such as Jagoroni Chakra Foundation will want to know whether Plan International keeps or grows its Cox's Bazar work.

What to watch

Any joint initiative with the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education on child marriage or girls' secondary schooling, and Plan International's funding plans for the Rohingya response in 2027.

Sources

  • Plan International CEO visits Bangladesh, calls for better education for girls, The Business Standard (press release), 13 November 2026
